instruction: Export the essay document "Recruitment_and_retention_of_health_professionals_across_Europe.docx" from /home/user to PDF format and save it as "Recruitment_and_retention.pdf" in the same directory.

metadata.explanation: Task requires exporting a LibreOffice Writer document to PDF format. The evaluator checks if the PDF file exists, has the correct page count (estimated 35 pages based on 8702 words), and contains the correct essay content. Verification includes: page count (±2 tolerance), word count (7500-9500 range), file size (>50KB), key content phrases (Recruitment, retention, health professional, Europe), and PDF metadata (LibreOffice producer).
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Score is weighted: 30% for page count match (33-37 pages), 20% for word count range (7500-9500), 10% for file size (>50KB), 30% for key content phrases (at least 3/4), 10% for LibreOffice metadata. Maximum score 1.0.

llm_judge_reasons: Comprehensive multi-dimensional verification: Evaluator checks page count (±2 tolerance), word count (7500-9500), file size (>50KB), key content phrases (Recruitment, retention, health professional, Europe), and LibreOffice metadata
Strong content verification: Extracts full PDF text and searches for 4 essay-specific key phrases, requiring at least 3/4 to be present (30% of score)
Robust word count validation: Ensures full content was exported by checking word count falls in 7500-9500 range (20% of score)
Gaming-resistant scoring: Multi-dimensional checks (5 different aspects) with weighted scoring prevent agents from passing with trivial/wrong PDFs
Metadata verification: Confirms PDF was created by LibreOffice, ensuring correct export tool was used (10% of score)
Appropriate tolerance: Page count allows ±2 pages for export variations, word count has reasonable range
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Consider making word count and file size thresholds configurable via expected.rules instead of hardcoding them in the metric function
Optional: Could add verification that source .docx filename appears in PDF metadata (if LibreOffice includes it), though current content verification is already strong
